lesson_text: The account's loss if the stop hits. Risk per trade is the money you plan to lose if the trade goes against you. It is measured against the whole account. Van Tharp's example: risking 1% of a $100,000 account puts $1,000 at risk. That is not the same as the money you put into the stock. Risk per trade is your planned loss at the stop, as a percent of the whole account.

lesson_text: Hold it and add no more shares. Our rule: the full size goes on at one price with one stop, and we never add. lesson_text: When, and how much, we trade. The reading is Green, Yellow, Orange or Red, and we check it before any stock. Green allows full risk per grade and up to 10 positions.
